schema: functions: name -> file, orig, instr (ours/original), status (same, close, open; measured by compare/cas/check.sh), lines (open: differing instructions), note (by hand); data: module -> differing data bytes.
compiler: sccvc -O (parser.y and assemble.c without -O), the working compiler of cas (OLDCC.md)
about:
/bin/cas was built by an older scc than the shipped one, which we do not have as such; sccvc is the nearest found (src/TODO.md, step 10): byte identity is not reached. The behaviour is the same: the corpus (`host/tools/corpus.sh cas`) and the tests of tools/test. The differences that are not differences of the source are the classes D1 ... D13 of `host/OLDCC.md`.

The compiler (measured 2026-11-09, the model in `progcfg.py`, `strictcmp.py` over the 155 functions): the shipped scc gives 2 functions strictly equal, 16 masked, 9228 differing lines; `sccvc` with `slibc-v11` 59 strictly equal, 59 masked, 2917 lines (2026-11-09), with the text, data and bss sizes of the original. Data: 36374 of 38360 bytes equal at the same address; the rest are code addresses in jump and pointer tables (they follow the code). Bit 31 of the addresses in `.addr` (also the jump tables, which the spopt of sccvc writes as `.addr`) comes from `OLD_D13`; the value lists of a cpir switch right in front of its targets from `OLD_D6T` (`OLDCC.md`). Its switches are those of the old compilers v0/v0p (`OLDCC.md`, section 2): /bin/cas was probably built by a segmented compiler of that age (a guess). The notes below are measured with sccvc. The data and bss sizes are those of the original since `slibc-v11` (the members that differ from the shipped slibc are cut from /bin/cas: `src/lib/oldslibc/*/0_2.s`, `host/tools/oldslibc_cas.py`).
